- **[P2] Mark resolver acceptance tests as Linux-only** — [test_openai_responses.py:479](/C:/Users/15492/.codex-clean/worktrees/ed95/QuantMesh/services/research_agent/tests/test_openai_responses.py:479) and [test_openai_responses.py:547](/C:/Users/15492/.codex-clean/worktrees/ed95/QuantMesh/services/research_agent/tests/test_openai_responses.py:547). Both tests run unconditionally, while `_OwnedResolverBackend.connect_tcp()` explicitly rejects non-Linux platforms. Windows/macOS runs therefore fail at the resolver-PID assertion or raise `ModelUnavailableError`. Add platform skips to these Linux acceptance fixtures; unsupported-platform refusal can remain a separate test.

The R1 DNS executor deadline finding is addressed by the owned resolver and cancellation kill/reap path. No further actionable Standards findings in the scoped provider, tests, README section, and Task1 plan.

- **[P2] The 30-second deadline excludes event-loop shutdown** — [openai_responses.py:315](/C:/Users/15492/.codex-clean/worktrees/ed95/QuantMesh/services/research_agent/src/qm_research_agent/openai_responses.py:315). `_exchange()` times out after 30 seconds, but `asyncio.run()` subsequently waits for its default executor to shut down. HTTP DNS resolution can use that executor; cancelling the coroutine cannot stop an already-running resolver thread. On CPython 3.12, shutdown can add up to 300 seconds, exceeding Task1’s transport deadline. The delayed-stream fixture only exercises cancellable async work. Bound the complete synchronous invocation, including resolver teardown, and add a stalled-resolution/shutdown fixture.

No other actionable Standards findings in the scoped files. Fixed-origin configuration, disabled environment discovery/redirects, streamed byte enforcement, response/client cleanup, strict normalization, existing gateway admission, and the factory’s $1 reservation appear consistent with Task1. Current official schema evidence resolves the cache-write-field concern.
